summary: NASA has announced plans to brief the public on Artemis program acceleration and the status of upcoming Moon missions, alongside advancing battery technologies and lander testing for lunar operations. In other civil space updates, the agency is preparing for milestone U.S. Spacewalks 100 and 101, while astronaut Christina Koch is stepping down from active duty following her Artemis II assignment. In military space, the Department of the Air Force consolidated 50 battle network programs into a single $4.5 billion contract vehicle, the U.S. Air Force tested a new Sentinel ICBM reentry vehicle, and the U.S. Space Force activated SPACEFOR-SOC as its service component command under U.S. Special Operations Command. Internationally, Japan’s space agency selected ArkEdge for two lunar navigation demonstrations, while the Japanese VERTECS nanosatellite completed initial operations and began scientific observations. On the commercial front, SpaceX delivered more than 6,000 pounds of cargo to the International Space Station, Reflect Orbital purchased two launches from Skyroot Aerospace, and Avio signed an agreement with Lockheed Martin for solid rocket motor production. In planetary science and Earth monitoring, researchers published new findings on white dwarf star colors and early-universe black holes, while NASA satellites tracked Amazon rainforest fires and Hurricane Simon off the Mexican coast. Readers should watch for the European Space Agency’s Hera probe to arrive at its target asteroid later this month to inspect the wreckage from NASA's DART mission.
